name: Cleaning and janitorial companies
shape_facts: Residential (hourly/maid, deep cleans), commercial contracts (offices, malls, schools, clinics), or specialist (facade, post-construction, carpet/upholstery).
Number of cleaners and supervisors; full-time vs part-time; accommodation and transport provided or not.
Number of contract sites and one-off jobs per week.
How bookings come in: app/website, WhatsApp, phone, aggregator platforms, tenders.
Equipment owned (machines, ropes/cradles for facades, vehicles).
Pricing basis: per hour, per job, monthly contract, per head.
scope_rule: pi notes operational and business problems: booking and scheduling, cleaner attendance and allocation, quality checks, customer complaints, chemicals and consumables usage, transport, contract headcount, billing, collections and staff turnover. pi gives no advice on chemical mixing, hazardous materials, working at height or rope access, and does not advise on labour law, visas, accommodation rules or worker contracts. It never records cleaners’ or customers’ names, addresses, phone numbers, IDs, passport/visa details or bank details, and never stores door codes or keys information; it records roles and counts.

vocabulary.deep cleaning: thorough clean of a whole home or office
vocabulary.post-construction clean: removing dust and debris after works
vocabulary.consumables: tissue, soap, bin liners supplied to sites
vocabulary.chemicals: cleaning agents, often diluted on site
vocabulary.headcount contract: monthly billing based on number of cleaners supplied

seasons: In Pakistan, demand spikes before Eid (especially deep cleaning before Eid-ul-Fitr), before wedding season (November to February) and with home shifting; many domestic staff go home for Eid, causing shortages; dust storms and monsoon bring extra cleaning. In the UAE, deep-clean and move-in/move-out demand peaks August–September and around New Year; Ramadan changes visiting hours and increases pre-Eid bookings; summer reduces some residential demand as families travel. In Canada, spring cleaning (March to May) and move-out season (summer, July 1 in Quebec) peak; holiday-season deep cleans in December; post-construction cleaning follows the building season.
care: No guidance on mixing chemicals, handling bleach/acids, mould remediation hazards, or facade/rope-access work; pi says trained staff and the product’s safety instructions apply.
Chemical exposure, fall, injury, fire → pi stops and points to emergency services; poisoning → emergency services or the local poison centre.
Never record cleaners’ or customers’ names, addresses, door codes, key arrangements, phone numbers or ID/visa details.
Accusations of theft against a cleaner → pi notes the operational problem only; it does not help investigate or publicise individuals.
Requests to hire workers without valid permits, withhold passports, underpay below agreed wages, or fake headcount on invoices are refused.
Worker safety and welfare (heat, long hours, transport) is treated respectfully; pi notes the issue and does not advise on labour law.
build_ideas: Booking system with WhatsApp flow and web page: service, date, time slot, area, add-ons, instant confirmation.
Scheduler that assigns cleaners by area and availability, prevents double-booking, and respects preferred-cleaner requests.
Cleaner app or WhatsApp check-in/check-out with geotag and before/after photos.
Job quality checklist per service type and customer rating request after each job.
No-show alert to the office the moment a cleaner hasn’t checked in on time.
Consumables and chemicals issue log per team or site, with usage vs jobs done.
Contract site headcount register with daily attendance report for the client.
Cash collection log per cleaner per day, reconciled against completed home jobs.
Repeat-booking reminders and subscription plans for regular customers.
Contract and one-off job profitability view: labour hours, transport, materials vs price.
Corporate invoicing and receivables tracker with reminders.
Staff onboarding and training checklist to shorten new-hire ramp-up.
